messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple GPU containers on gpu-node-12 reporting CUDA illegal memory access; node is flapping, OOM churn observed. severity: P1. Paging activity spike recorded. Paging events correlated with serving runtime restarts. Triggering oncall.
sofia (oncall): I'm looking. any customer impact yet?
AJ: 5xx spike on /v1/generate starting ~12:02 UTC, error rate ~18% for last 3m. Top affected region: us-west1.
Devon: confirmed node kubelet restarted twice in 6m. dmesg shows kernel reporting device pagewalk faults.
Mira S.: pushing logs now. quick grep shows repeated "NVRM: Xid 31" entries and a few "cuda: illegal memory access" from the runtime.
kevin-ops: graph shows eviction pressure on gpu-node-12, swap-in rate high -> heavy pagewalks. suspect a rare page-table walk race with latest nvidia driver.
sofia (oncall): assign owners: @Devon take runtime triage, @AJ own traffic mitigation + routing, @Mira handle logs + customer comms. I'll coordinate with infra.
Devon: triage notes: container crashes appear correlated with long-running KV cache fills; while prefetching, we see misaligned pte hits and then an illegal mem access in lmm-service. Repro steps attempted on canary failed (hard to repro). stack snippet:
```
lmm-service[pid=8421]: GPU kernel launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
backtrace:
  0x7f9d1a2c runtime.cu:0x3f
  0x7f9d1a8d kv_cache.cu:0xa1
  0x7f9d1b0b exec.cu:0x2f
```
Devon: also seeing kernel log:
```
[ 12.02.34 ] NVRM: Xid (0000:03:00): 31, pid=8421, GPU 00000000:03:00.0: Ch ID 234. Illegal memory access during page table walk
```
AJ: mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic from gpu-node-12 -> spin up extra instances in us-west1-d 2) route heavy KV-cache workloads to Dedicated pool fallback 3) temporary autoscale down canary to reduce pressure. Starting reroute now.
Mira S.: customer ops: AcmeCorp requests status — their job failures match our 12:02 window. preparing a short note.
sofia (oncall): infra observation: memory fragmentation on node high, plus kernel 5.15 + driver 525 combination on that node. Rolling the node to older driver might help but that's intrusive.
infra-bot: Started cordon/drain for gpu-node-12 by @sofia (oncall).
kevin-ops: quick live mitigation we can try: disable kernel page-fault on GPU (uvm) softprefetch? Not ideal. Alternative: set container runtime to `--oom-kill-disable=false`? hmm.
Devon: trying a runtime patch: turn off prefetching in KV cache for model-serving processes on that host. Patching config and restarting lmm-service on node-12.
AJ: traffic reroute progress: shifted ~60% of traffic off node-12, 5xx rate falling to 4%. still seeing tail latency increases.
Mira S.: AcmeCorp: "We saw 20% failed requests during 12:02-12:10, some requests retried client-side and recovered." sending interim update.
sofia (oncall): root cause hypothesis: rare node driver + large-pagewalk workload => TLB/pagewalk corner-case causing kernel to return bad physical mapping leading to CUDA illegal access in user GPU kernel. Could be a kernel/driver race under high fragmentation.
Devon: for safety, we're hotpatching serving runtime to disable the aggressive KV prefetch on node-12 and restarting containers. If that reduces pagewalks we have a reproducible mitigation.
Mira S.: doing canary deploy of config change to two replicas on node-12 now.
kevin-ops: also increasing node-level vm.min_free_kbytes and clearing pagecache on drained containers.
infra-bot: Drain complete for gpu-node-12; node cordoned.
AJ: traffic now 95% off node-12. 5xx at 1.2%, back to baseline for most customers. keeping watch for 10m.
Devon: after restart with prefetch disabled, containers on node-12 have been stable for 7m. logs show no new NVRM Xid entries.
Mira S.: customer update sent to AcmeCorp and two other customers impacted. CS will follow up for detailed postmortem.
sofia (oncall): next actions: 1) collect full kernel logs and dmesg/oom logs from node-12 2) reproduce on repro-cluster with same driver/kernel/fragmentation 3) consider driver rollback if repro succeeded 4) longer term: add workload safeguards to avoid aggressive prefetch under high fragmentation.
AJ: opened temporary incident-ops runbook entry for routing in similar GPU node flaps.
Devon: recording hashes, stack traces, and config used for the live mitigation. Will attach to the incident tracker.
Mira S.: final customer note scheduled to send when we have repro confirmation.
sofia (oncall): marking as "mitigated" for now. leave open until we have root cause and postmortem. thanks team :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> residual monitoring for 1h. assigned to Devon for root cause / postmortem.
